paragraphs.source_en: Upon reaching Imamura, Kutsukake Castle was already close at hand. Imagawa Yoshimoto advanced with the utmost caution. Whenever he passed through a village, he sent men ahead to sound out the inhabitants and had his palanquin proceed only after they confirmed that nothing was amiss. This was because, before the campaign began, Matsudaira Motoyasu had warned him that the people of this region would fiercely resist the Imagawa army.

paragraphs.source_en: Beneath his Shokkō brocade armor, he wore a white battle robe. His long sword, two shaku and six sun in length, was his treasured Sōza Samonji, while at his waist he wore the heirloom dagger Matsukura Gō Yoshihiro. Yoshimoto's corpulent body made it impossible for him to mount a horse, so he sat at ease in a palanquin inlaid with gold and silver. From time to time he opened his eyes to survey his surroundings, continually wiping away the sweat that streamed from him.

paragraphs.source_en: They had spent the sixteenth and seventeenth at Okazaki Castle, making their final preparations for battle.
